diagnostic_approaches.name: Radiographic size-based malignancy risk estimation for pulmonary nodules
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Estimate malignancy risk based on nodule size on CT
criteria_or_scoring: Probability of malignancy for nodules <6 mm around 1% [cite: 403]
For those 6–8 mm between 1% and 2% [cite: 403]
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Take into consideration size, density, location, edge characteristics, calcification, and changes between serial scans. [cite: 402]
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Smaller nodules are more likely to be benign. [cite: 403]
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Initial radiographic assessment to guide malignancy risk.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: Smaller nodules are more likely to be benign, with the probability of malignancy for nodules <6 mm around 1%, and for those 6–8 mm between 1% and 2%

diagnostic_approaches.name: Volume doubling time (VDT) assessment on serial imaging
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Differentiate benign from malignant nodules using growth rate
criteria_or_scoring: Rapid VDT (<30 days) or very long VDT (>400 days) suggests benignity [cite: 411]
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Compare serial CT volumes; growth is typically ≥25% volume increase. [cite: 622]
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Malignant nodules often have VDT 30–500 days. [cite: 412]
diagnostic_approaches.limitations: Assumes exponential growth; not accurate for all tumors. [cite: 623]
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: Benign IPNs tend to have ... rapid volume doubling time (<30 days) or a very long volume doubling time (>400 days). Malignant nodules ... have a volume doubling time of between 30 and 500 days.

diagnostic_approaches.name: Nodule margin characteristics classification (radiographic)
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Classify nodule edge features associated with benign vs malignant etiologies
criteria_or_scoring: Smooth, well defined [cite: 426]
Irregular, Lobulated, Spiculated [cite: 426]
Sunburst or corona radiata appearance [cite: 426]
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: Margin Smooth, well defined Irregular, Lobulated Spiculated Sunburst or corona radiata appearance

diagnostic_approaches.name: Nodule density classification: solid vs subsolid (including part-solid and ground glass)
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Stratify risk based on nodule density and its temporal behavior
criteria_or_scoring: Solid nodules: higher malignancy risk with larger size, irregular/spiculated margins, and VDT 30–500 days [cite: 412]
Subsolid nodules (SSNs): part-solid and ground glass [cite: 404]
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Part-solid nodules increase risk as the solid component grows. [cite: 418]
diagnostic_approaches.limitations: TTNB yield and PET sensitivity are lower in SSNs unless the solid component is larger. [cite: 419]
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: Nodules are divided into two categories, solid and subsolid, with subsolid nodules (SSNs) further classified into part-solid and ground glass.

diagnostic_approaches.name: SSN behavior over time
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Use change in the solid component to guide management
criteria_or_scoring: Larger solid component → higher malignancy risk [cite: 417]
Growth of the solid component increases malignancy risk even if overall size unchanged [cite: 418]
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Serial CT assessment of the solid component.
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Growth triggers a more aggressive diagnostic approach. [cite: 429]
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: Even if the overall size ... the risk of malignancy increases if the solid component grows.

diagnostic_approaches.name: FDG-PET for malignancy risk stratification
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Functional imaging to help distinguish malignant from benign nodules
criteria_or_scoring: SUV ≥2.5 suggests inflammatory, infectious, or malignant process [cite: 452]
Descriptive uptake (absent/mild/moderate/high) or SUV value [cite: 451]
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Obtain PET/CT and interpret uptake patterns.
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: PET improves localization of malignant lesions but has false positives/negatives. [cite: 450, 433]
diagnostic_approaches.limitations: Lower sensitivity in endemic infectious settings; false negatives for small lesions, carcinoid, MIA, AIS, pure GGNs. [cite: 449, 436, 437, 438]
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: Updated meta-analysis ... sensitivity of 89% and specificity of 75% for diagnosing lung cancer ...

diagnostic_approaches.name: Pure ground glass nodule prognosis (surgical series)
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Context for management of pure GGNs
criteria_or_scoring: Pathology may be AAH, in situ carcinoma, or well-differentiated adenocarcinoma [cite: 430]
100% 5-year survival for malignant pure GGNs in a resected series [cite: 431]
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: When considering intervention for pure GGNs.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: A study of 704 patients ... reported a 100% 5-year survival for malignant pure GGNs.

diagnostic_approaches.name: Volumetric assessment and doubling time
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Increase accuracy of benign vs malignant discrimination
criteria_or_scoring: Growth defined as ≥25% volume increase [cite: 622]
VDT <500 days typical for malignant nodules; benign median 947 days [cite: 624]
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Use software volumetrics on serial low-dose CTs. [cite: 619]
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Adds ~20% predictive value when combined with risk models. [cite: 626]
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: Using a cutoff of 500 days ... specificity 90%, sensitivity 91%, NPV 98%, PPV 67%.

diagnostic_approaches.name: Blood-based rule-out proteomic biomarker (LG3BP, C163A + clinical factors)
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Reduce invasive procedures in benign disease
criteria_or_scoring: Intermediate-risk IPNs 8–30 mm [cite: 647]
Combines two proteins with clinical factors (age, smoking, nodule diameter, edge, lobe) [cite: 647]
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Obtain blood test and integrate with clinical model.
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: High sensitivity and NPV support surveillance in low-likelihood malignancy. [cite: 647]
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: Sensitivity of 97%, specificity of 44%, NPV 98% in intermediate-risk.

diagnostic_approaches.name: Nasal swab genomic classifier
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Noninvasive rule-out and rule-in for smokers with IPNs
criteria_or_scoring: Low-risk classifier: sensitivity 96%, specificity 42% [cite: 652]
High-risk classifier: sensitivity 58%, specificity 90% [cite: 652]
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Can reclassify management in intermediate-risk nodules.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: Low-risk classifier sensitivity 96% and specificity 42% ... high-risk sensitivity 58% and specificity 90%.

diagnostic_approaches.name: VERITAS trial: Nav bronchoscopy vs TTNB in pCA >10% IPNs
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Compare diagnostic yield and complication rate
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Equivalent yield (~76%); nav bronchoscopy had fewer complications (5.8% vs 31%). [cite: 668]
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: Diagnostic yield equivalent (76%); significantly fewer complications with navigational bronchoscopy.

diagnostic_approaches.name: EBUS diagnostic yield (mediastinal nodes) vs pCA
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Yield increases with higher pretest probability
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Highest yield ~80% for mediastinal EBUS; positive results 77% when pCA >60%. [cite: 663, 666]
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Staging or central nodes in suspected lung cancer.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: EBUS had highest diagnostic yield at 80% ... positive result 77% when pCA >60%.

diagnostic_approaches.name: Guided bronchoscopy diagnostic yield and safety overview
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Summarize pooled yields and safety for guided bronchoscopy across modalities
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: The pooled diagnostic yield for peripheral IPNs across all bronchoscopic modalities was 69%, a figure that has not improved over 20 years. [cite: 671] [cite_start]Factors that may improve yield include larger lesion size and the presence of a bronchus sign. [cite: 673] [cite_start]The overall pneumothorax rate is approximately 2%. [cite: 674]
diagnostic_approaches.limitations: Varying prevalence of malignancy across studies impacts the reported diagnostic yield. [cite: 672]
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Modality selection and patient counseling for peripheral lesions.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: Pooled diagnostic yield across all bronchoscopic modalities was 69%, which had not improved over 20 years.

steps: Low pCA: surveillance with noncontrast low-dose CT; consider volumetrics. [cite: 515, 581, 606]
Intermediate pCA: PET/CT and/or nonsurgical biopsy (CT-guided or bronchoscopy) depending on lesion factors. [cite: 521]
High pCA (>65% ACCP; >70% BTS): surgical diagnosis; [cite_start]PET/CT for staging. [cite: 525, 528, 581]
notes: For SSNs, management is driven by solid component size/growth. [cite: 416, 429]
PET is usually not recommended if the solid component is <8 mm. [cite: 428, 540]
treatment_algorithms.source_excerpt: Guidelines provide recommendations ... incorporate pCA and lesion characteristics.

clinical_guidelines.title: American College of Chest Physicians Guidelines – Solid Nodules
specific_recommendations: Low-risk IPNs (pCA <5%): manage with surveillance. [cite: 514]
In patients with solid nodules <8 mm and without risk factors, choose CT surveillance based on nodule size. [cite: 516]
If multiple nodules are present, base follow-up on the size of the largest nodule. [cite: 517]
For solid nodules >8 mm with very low risk (<5% pCA): serial surveillance imaging at 3–6, 9–12, and 18–24 months. [cite: 518]
If a solid lesion is stable for 2 years, no further CT imaging is required. [cite: 519]
Intermediate risk (pCA 5–65%): further evaluate with PET scan or nonsurgical biopsy (CT-guided or bronchoscopy depending on nodule factors). [cite: 521, 522]
If pretest probability is <30–40% and the lesion is not PET avid or a needle biopsy is nondiagnostic and the lesion is not PET avid, surveillance CT is advised. [cite: 523]
High risk (pCA >65%): do not use functional imaging solely to characterize; pursue surgical diagnosis. [cite: 525, 527]
Consider nonsurgical biopsy before surgery if tumor mutational analysis is recommended (clinical stage 1B–3A). [cite: 527]
Obtain PET imaging prior to treatment for lung cancer staging. [cite: 528]
If lesion grows on surveillance, perform nonsurgical biopsy or surgical resection unless comorbidities preclude these and SBRT is being considered without tissue confirmation. [cite: 529]
Consider surgical diagnosis if the nodule is PET avid or nonsurgical biopsy is suspicious for malignancy. [cite: 530]
Shared decision-making should be performed throughout care. [cite: 531]

decision_points_and_pathways.pathway: CT surveillance intervals per nodule size; largest nodule dictates follow-up when multiple are present. [cite: 516, 517]
decision_points_and_pathways.source_excerpt: In patients with solid nodules less than 8 mm ...

clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: ACCP Guidelines provide recommendations for the management of solid and subsolid IPNs.

clinical_guidelines.title: American College of Chest Physicians Guidelines – Subsolid Nodules
clinical_guidelines.condition: Indeterminate pulmonary nodules (subsolid nodules, including pure ground glass and part-solid)
specific_recommendations: Pure ground glass nodule <5 mm: no further follow-up. [cite: 535]
Pure ground glass nodule >5 mm: annual surveillance for at least 3 years. [cite: 536]
Part solid is defined as >50% ground glass. [cite: 538]
Part-solid <8 mm: repeat CT at 3, 12, and 24 months, then annual scans for an additional 1–3 years. [cite: 538]
Part-solid >8 mm: repeat CT in 3 months; if persistent and/or growing, evaluate with PET, biopsy, or resection. [cite: 539]
Do not perform PET when the solid component is <8 mm. [cite: 540]
Part-solid >15 mm: evaluate with PET, nonsurgical biopsy, or resection. [cite: 541]

decision_points_and_pathways.source_excerpt: pure ground glass nodule less than 5 mm in diameter, no further follow-up is recommended.

decision_points_and_pathways.pathway: CT at 3, 12, 24 months then annual 1–3 years
decision_points_and_pathways.source_excerpt: Part-solid nodules that are less than 8 mm ...

decision_points_and_pathways.pathway: Reimage at 3 months; if persistent/growing, PET/biopsy/resection
decision_points_and_pathways.source_excerpt: Part-solid >8 mm ... PET, biopsy, or resection; >15 mm warrants further evaluation

clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: Subsolid nodules (pure ground glass and part-solid)
contraindications_and_exceptions: Avoid PET when the solid component is <8 mm. [cite: 540]
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: ACCP Guidelines provide recommendations for the management of solid and subsolid IPNs.

clinical_guidelines.title: British Thoracic Society (BTS) Guidelines
specific_recommendations: Utilize the Brock and Herder models to assess pCA. [cite: 580]
Risk thresholds differ from ACCP: low (<10%), intermediate (10-70%), and high (>70%). [cite: 581]
Do not surveil nodules <5 mm or <80 mm³. [cite: 581]
For solid nodules with low pCA (<10%), recommend repeat CT with volumetric assessment. [cite: 585]
A VDT <400 days warrants further investigation. [cite: 586]
A surveillance period of one year is sufficient if risk is low (<10%). [cite: 582]
For solid nodules with pCA >10% and a solid component >8mm, pursue PET/CT. [cite: 592]
For SSNs >5 mm, risk stratify with the Brock model. [cite: 598]
For SSNs with pCA <10%, repeat CT at 1, 2, and 4 years. [cite: 599]
Resection or nonsurgical treatment is recommended for part-solid nodules if the solid component enlarges or develops. [cite: 601]
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: The British Thoracic Society (BTS) Guidelines echo many of the recommendations put forth in the ACCP guidelines.

clinical_guidelines.title: Fleischner Society Guidelines
specific_recommendations: Guidelines are for incidentally detected IPNs, not screen-detected nodules. [cite: 604]
Aims to limit evaluation for patients with <1% probability of lung cancer. [cite: 603]
Recommends assigning risk categories to determine the need for CT surveillance, PET, or tissue sampling. [cite: 606]
Provides surveillance intervals for high-risk patients with nodules <6 mm. [cite: 607]
Recommends risk categorization for nodules >8 mm. [cite: 607]
contraindications_and_exceptions: Not for use in screen-detected nodules. [cite: 604]
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: The Fleischner Society Guidelines aim to limit unnecessary evaluation of patients with less than 1% probability of lung cancer...
